stages.name: championship_group
stages.note: places 1-6; title decided on total points including the regular season

stages.name: placement_playoff
stages.note: places 7-10: 7v10, 8v9, final; winner gets CZK 3m and a better Czech Cup seed, no European place since 2023-24

playoff.entries: 15th and 14th of the Chance Liga vs 2nd and 3rd of the Chance Národní liga
playoff.note: two separate two-leg ties; 16th is relegated directly, 13th is always safe

playoff.entries: 2nd and 3rd of the Chance Národní liga vs 15th and 14th of the Chance Liga
playoff.note: champion is promoted directly; only the two play-off winners go up

stages.name: promotion_baraz
stages.note: winners of groups A and B play for the single promotion place

playoff.entries: winner of group A vs winner of group B
playoff.note: one promotion place; the loser stays at level 3. In 2025-26 both group winners went up because the Národní liga had extra vacancies

boundaries.note: Národní liga: champion up, 2nd and 3rd into two-leg play-outs. Chance Liga: 16th down, 15th and 14th into the same play-outs, 13th safe. Both ties two legs, no away-goals rule.

Národní liga sends its bottom 2 down, each to ČFL or MSFL by regional affiliation (0-2 to either). Up: MSFL champion directly, ČFL only through a two-leg baráž between its group A and B winners. Net level-3 size is fixed at 32 + 18.

conflicts.note: The size is right; the shape is not. It is one division split into two 16-team groups whose winners meet in a two-leg baráž for a single promotion place.
The split is three-way, not two-way. Places 7-10 play a two-legged placement bracket (7v10, 8v9, final), not a relegation group.

conflicts.ours: two parallel leagues: Bohemian and Moravian-Silesian
conflicts.note: There are two level-3 competitions but three groups. Our CZ3C row bundles the two Bohemian groups; CZ3M is the single Moravian-Silesian league.
Any model that relegates a flat bottom 3 from the Chance Liga is wrong for this format.

notes: Both top divisions are 16 clubs / 30 rounds; level 3 is 32 + 18. Points are never halved at the split. Relegation counts below level 2 are not fixed numbers: ČFL drops 2-4 and MSFL 0-2 depending on where the Národní liga's two relegated clubs belong, and both are fed by Divize winners (level 4, outside this model). 2026-27 movement shows the rules in action but is not the rule: Dukla Praha was the only direct relegation from the Chance Liga (16th), Karviná was administratively moved down for the 2022-24 corruption case (Ethics Committee, no appeal) and its spot was offered to Táborsko (refused) then Artis Brno; Zbrojovka Brno went up as Národní liga champion, and the Národní liga lost Sparta B plus České Budějovice and Chrudim for failing licensing, so three level-3 clubs came up (Kladno and Arsenal Česká Lípa from ČFL, Třinec from MSFL) instead of the usual two.
